findings.existing_code: if len(set(aliases.values())) != len(aliases) or any(not _ROLE.fullmatch(alias) for alias in aliases.values()):
findings.description: `legacy_role_aliases` values are validated against `_ROLE` (line 39, `^(agent|service)-[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`), but migration-map.schema.json declares them as `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*$`, and the pre-migration seeder created AppRoles named by bare agent name (e.g. `codex-cloud`). Any real legacy alias fails preflight with 'invalid or colliding legacy role alias'. Because the cutover guard (lines 279-285) refuses when any AppRole outside `owned_retirements` still carries `coordinator-read`, an operator can never confirm cutover on a deployment that has the old roles without deleting them by hand outside the audited path. No unit test and no live smoke exercises aliases.
findings.resolution: Validate aliases with the schema's slug pattern and add a test where a bare-name legacy alias is retired during cutover.

findings.description: Runtime schema validation (every plan, audit event, and bundle) reads schemas from the literal `openspec/changes/<change-id>/contracts` directory. Archival moves it to `openspec/changes/archive/<date>-<id>/`, so `make bao-seed` and every apply will raise FileNotFoundError once the change lands. `parents[3]` is also wrong for the `install.sh` runtime copies under `.claude/skills/`. AGENTS.md forbids pinning this path even in tests.
findings.resolution: Ship the schemas as package data in `openbao-credentials` or resolve via change_dir()-style discovery; add a test that validation works with the change directory absent.

findings.description: The rewritten seeder never writes `retained_internal` keys anywhere. The previous seeder populated `secret/coordinator` from `.secrets.yaml`, and the dev server from `make bao-dev` is ephemeral, so nothing now seeds the internal document that `_load_secrets()`, `langfuse_env.sh`, and `_verify_internal_handoff` (reads `coordinator` with raise_on_deleted_version) depend on. In a fresh dev environment cutover cannot be verified and internal Bao interpolation silently disappears from the dev workflow. D3/D5 are ambiguous on whether 'retained for internal use' means written or merely left alone; needs a plan-owner decision.
findings.resolution: Either write retained_internal keys to `<mount>/coordinator` or document a separate internal-seeding step for bao-dev; record the choice in the choices ledger.

findings.description: Within one --confirm-cutover invocation the seeder re-points the internal AppRole, proves a fresh login works, and immediately deletes `coordinator-read`. Tokens already issued to a running coordinator or langfuse helper still carry the old policy name, so deleting it strips their read capability until re-login. D6 orders 'cut over consumers, observe reload, then retire'; collapsing install-and-retire into one step removes that window.
findings.resolution: Gate `coordinator-read` deletion behind a second explicit step or document that cutover requires internal-loader restart in the same window.

findings.description: No test exercises `legacy_role_aliases` (preflight, preview, or retirement), which is why finding 1 escaped. The only cutover test stubs `_verify_internal_handoff`, so the 'internal policy proven before shared policy deletion' ordering is asserted only by mock-call index.
findings.resolution: Add a cutover test with a bare-name legacy alias, and one leaving `_verify_internal_handoff` live with a mocked hvac.Client to assert it runs between the internal role update and delete_policy.

findings.description: Internal-only policy and handoff read hardcode `coordinator`, while the internal loader (D5, OpenBaoConfig) still honors `BAO_SECRET_PATH` and the previous seeder derived its policy from it. A non-default BAO_SECRET_PATH deployment gets a policy for the wrong path and a handoff that can never pass. Fails closed, so not a blocker.
findings.resolution: Read BAO_SECRET_PATH (default coordinator) for both the policy path and the handoff read, validated by the mount segment regex.

findings.description: `_validate_schema` embeds the first jsonschema error message. For bootstrap-bundle validation jsonschema quotes the offending instance value on type/minLength failures, so a malformed server response (non-string token or role_id) would put x-sensitive material into the traceback main() lets reach stderr.
findings.resolution: For the bundle report only json_path/validator, not error.message.

findings.description: Principal roles set secret_id_num_uses=1 but no secret_id_ttl. Every apply issues a fresh wrapped SecretID and overwrites the previous bundle; an unconsumed prior SecretID stays valid server-side indefinitely after its 300s wrapping token expires, accumulating across re-seeds.
findings.resolution: Set secret_id_ttl to a small multiple of the wrap TTL.

findings.description: Managed state is written only after all mutations succeed. If apply fails after creating roles/policies/paths for newly keyed agents, those resources exist in Bao but are unrecorded, so a later registry removal never retires them.
findings.resolution: Record ownership before mutation and drop retired names only after deletion succeeds.

findings.description: OpenBao reports `options: null` for KV-v1 and several non-KV mounts; `mount.get('options', {})` returns None in that case, so preflight raises AttributeError instead of the intended 'configured mount is not KV-v2' ValueError (CFG-16).

seed_secrets/seed_approles/seed_db_engine are unreachable from the CLI but remain (still tested), and --with-db-engine is gone. The module docstring (lines 1-22), skills/bao-vault/SKILL.md, docs/openbao-secret-management.md, and .secrets.yaml.example still document the removed invocation, and the main agent-identity spec still names `bao-seed.py --with-db-engine` as the database-engine provisioning path, which the delta does not modify. Docs/SKILL.md are outside this package's write scope.
findings.resolution: Delete dead functions and tests (or keep a separate db-engine subcommand), fix the docstring in scope, route doc/spec updates to wp-integration.

findings.existing_code: bao-dev: ## Start OpenBao dev server and reconcile from an explicit migration map
findings.description: bao-dev starts the container and waits up to 15s before delegating to bao-seed, where the required-variable check lives; plain `make bao-dev` leaves a running empty OpenBao and then errors.
findings.resolution: Move the two `test -n` guards to a shared prerequisite target so bao-dev fails fast.

findings.description: Enabling the AppRole auth method is audited as openbao.principal.created for the identity-reader with resource `role`, misattributing a mount-level mutation to one principal. The event schema has no mount resource, so this is a contract limitation, not a code error.
findings.resolution: Accept; consider a `mount` resource value in a future contract revision.
